paras: The attempted lynching of Voscamp was a near-lynching in Michigan in which a man said to have murdered Lyman Cady near Coopersville 'narrowly escaped lynching by an infuriated gang of Cady's neighbors.' The episode was reported in late August 1881, when he was taken to Grand Rapids for safe-keeping. It survives only as one sentence in a syndicated column of state news.

According to the item, Voscamp, whose first name and race are not given, had killed Lyman Cady near Coopersville 'some months ago.' The column stated the killing as fact and reported no arrest, examination or charge.

Cady's neighbors, described as 'an infuriated gang,' came close to lynching Voscamp, but the item gives no date, place, number or account of what the gang did. He escaped, and he was afterward 'taken to Grand Rapids for safe-keeping,' which suggests he was then in official custody.
No report of an arrest of anyone in the gang, or of a trial of Voscamp for Cady's death, appears in the coverage.

The Lake County Star of Chase, Michigan, ran the item on August 25, 1881, in its 'News of the Week' column under 'Michigan,' and The Owosso Times printed the identical sentence the next day. The sentence sat between an item on a Grand Haven shooting and a baseball score, with no headline or comment. It called Voscamp 'the man who murdered Lyman Cady' without qualification, mentioned no race, and treated the mob as a passing detail of his removal to Grand Rapids.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Voscamp
bases: The only report says Voscamp 'narrowly escaped lynching by an infuriated gang' of the dead man's neighbors, a threatened mob killing that did not take place (A1).
Voscamp escaped the 'infuriated gang' and was alive and in custody at Grand Rapids, so no one was killed; the gang's size is not given, and its motive was the murder of Lyman Cady (A1).
One news-of-the-week item, run word for word in a second paper's copy of the same column, is the only report; no independent account was found (A1, A2).
